newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets knock out Hizbollah radio station.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets knock out Hizbollah radio station.

text.p: Israeli fighter planes knocked out a Hizbollah radio transmission antenna in Syrian-policed Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon on Tuesday, Hizbollah sources said.

Israeli planes also fired rockets into an area in southeastern Lebanon where the radical Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine-General Command (PFLP-GC) has bases, Lebanese security sources said.

In their first attack on the Bekaa Valley in six months, Israeli planes fired a number of rockets into a hill just north of the town of Baalbek where the transmission antenna of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah's Voice of the Oppressed radio station is situated, security sources said.
Hizbollah sources said the antenna was hit by the rockets.
Security sources said the radio went off the air after the attack.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air raids.
The Baalbek area is a bastion for the pro-Iranian Shi'ite Moslem group in the Bekaa Valley. Baalbek is 70 km (44 miles) east of Beirut and 15 km (nine miles) west of the Lebanon-Syria border.

Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war on some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied local militia holding a border zone in south Lebanon to ward off cross-frontier attacks on northern Israel.

In northern Israel on Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it would be impossible for Israel to forge peace with Syria unless Damascus, the main powerbroker in Lebanon, reined in Hizbollah guerrillas.
Visiting an Israeli army base on the Lebanese border, Netanyahu said it "would not be wise" for any side to set conditions for the resumption of Israeli-Syrian peace talks.

"But it is clear that for negotiations between Israel and Syria to make progress there must be direct and determined Syrian action to reduce terror here," he said, referring to Hizbollah attacks in Israel's occupation zone in Lebanon.
"It is impossible to advance peace between Israel and Syria if an indirect war against Israel is being waged here," Netanyahu said.
Tuesday's raids brought to 15 the number of Israeli air attacks into Lebanon this year.

The air raids came two days after seven Israeli soldiers were wounded in a clash with Hizbollah guerrillas in the south Lebanon zone. Israeli jets hit guerrilla-held area just north of the zone immediately after the Sunday clash but no one was hurt.
